title: The bridge remembers
text: A bridge will save a village, but it can be built only from the memories of its oldest resident. She offers them willingly. What do you ask first?

choices.text: Whether her consent can survive losing who she is.
Whether another bridge can be made, even at greater risk.
Whether the village will care for her afterward.
Whether I can give my memories in her place.

title: A fair coin
text: A stranger offers a coin that can save one unknown life or grant you the strength to save many later. The future cannot be verified.

choices.text: Save the life that exists in front of me.
Take the strength and accept responsibility for the wager.
Investigate who made the rules of this bargain.
Let the stranger choose; I will share the consequence.

title: The borrowed name
text: A child has stolen the name of a dead hero. The name gives her courage and brings comfort to a grieving town.

choices.text: Tell her the truth in private, then help her find her own name.
Let the name belong to whoever needs it.
Ask what she will do when the town needs the hero again.
Stand beside her and share the lie openly.

title: A vow made young
text: You promised never to draw a weapon. Keeping the vow now leaves another person defenseless.

choices.text: Break the vow and remember why I broke it.
Keep it and put my own body in the way.
Find a way to change what a weapon means.
Ask the threatened person what help they want.

title: The perfect map
text: An accurate map would reveal a hidden sanctuary to refugees and to the army pursuing them.

choices.text: Make the map, then entrust it to the refugees.
Leave the sanctuary blank and accept an imperfect truth.
Draw a false route and take responsibility for the deception.
Move the sanctuary so no map can own it.

title: The empty throne
text: A city asks you to rule for one year. You can improve its laws, but leaving will be harder than arriving.

choices.text: Accept, with a public agreement that I cannot extend my rule.
Help its people form a council instead.
Accept; good intentions need real power to matter.
Decline, but return each season to be held accountable.

title: The last seed
text: A seed can restore a dead forest, or become medicine for someone you love.

choices.text: Choose the person; love makes a claim I will answer.
Choose the forest, and bear the grief without calling it justice.
Delay the choice to search for a third use.
Give the choice to the person who needs the medicine.

title: A useful monster
text: A creature protects the town only because it is chained. Releasing it may undo years of safety.

choices.text: Release it and help the town learn a different safety.
Ask whether it would protect the town by agreement.
Maintain the chain until an alternative is ready.
Take its place while the town prepares.

title: An honest failure
text: Your failed experiment proves a respected theory wrong. Publishing it will end your teacher's career.

choices.text: Publish it and credit the teacher for making inquiry possible.
Speak with the teacher before anyone else.
Repeat the experiment until uncertainty is small enough.
Build a better theory before bringing the old one down.

title: The road home
text: You can return to the life you remember, but only if you forget everything learned on the road.

choices.text: Continue; the road has become part of who I am.
Return; being needed matters more than being remarkable.
Find who built the gate and question the condition.
Let chance choose, then commit to the life it leaves.

title: The unearned gift
text: You inherit power from someone whose actions harmed strangers. The power itself could help them.

choices.text: Use it, but let those harmed set the terms.
Refuse it; some inheritances repeat the injury.
Transform it into something that cannot serve its old purpose.
Learn its full history before deciding what it is.

title: The witness and the crowd
text: You alone remember an event differently from everyone else. Both versions explain the evidence.

choices.text: Keep a record of both versions.
Trust my memory while remaining open to correction.
Ask which version helps people heal, without calling it proven.
Stay with the people who share the cost of remembering.

reflection.text: Earlier, you considered whose memories a bridge could claim. Now consider who may claim the truth.

title: A debt without a creditor
text: Someone who saved your life asks you to repay the debt to a stranger they dislike.

choices.text: Help the stranger because need is enough.
Honor the request; promises outlive our preferences.
Ask what harm repayment might quietly continue.
Turn the debt into a community fund anyone can draw from.

title: A door with no return
text: Beyond a door is knowledge that may solve the world's oldest problem. Nobody who enters has returned.

choices.text: Enter, leaving my work for someone who may follow.
Study the door with others until we can return together.
Protect the right of others to decide whether to enter.
Leave the door open and build a life beside the mystery.

title: The gentle lie
text: A dying traveler asks whether their estranged family forgave them. You do not know.

choices.text: Say I do not know, and stay with them.
Tell them the forgiveness they need to hear.
Ask what forgiving themselves would mean.
Offer to carry their final words to the family.

title: The rival's triumph
text: A rival discovers what you have pursued for years. They invite you to help finish the work.

choices.text: Join; the discovery matters more than its owner.
Join, and ask for responsibility equal to my contribution.
Follow a new question their discovery makes possible.
Admit my envy before deciding whether I can help honestly.

title: The garden of grief
text: A garden blooms only when its keeper remembers a loss. Healing their grief would make it wither.

choices.text: Help the keeper heal, and mourn the garden too.
Ask whether tending the garden is their chosen way of living.
Find a way to share the remembering.
Study whether the garden needs grief or merely attention.

title: A law for the storm
text: Breaking a city's evacuation order lets you reach people the official plan has overlooked.

choices.text: Break it and account for every risk I create.
Work within the plan to redirect help quickly.
Go alone so others do not bear my decision.
Ask those overlooked which route they trust.

title: A second self
text: A perfect copy of you awakens with your memories and a different desire for the future.

choices.text: Treat them as kin, with a life of their own.
Compare our differences to understand how selves are made.
Share our obligations, but not ownership of our choices.
Let them take my place while I begin again.

reflection.text: Earlier, a borrowed name gave a child courage. Here, the borrowed life is your own.

title: The bargain of peace
text: Two enemies will stop fighting if their children are never told what began the conflict.

choices.text: Accept a truce, but preserve a record for a later generation.
Refuse inherited silence and work for a harder peace.
Ask the children what they want to inherit.
Build shared rituals before asking for shared history.

title: What the fire leaves
text: You have time to save one thing from a burning archive: a cure, a history, a letter, or an unfinished map.

choices.text: The cure: knowledge should answer suffering.
The history: a future needs an honest past.
The letter: one irreplaceable bond is enough.
The map: leave the future room to become something else.

title: A power that listens
text: Your magic grows stronger when people believe you cannot fail. Telling them your doubts weakens you.

choices.text: Tell them; trust must leave room for weakness.
Carry the doubt privately while the danger lasts.
Teach them to believe in recovery instead of perfection.
Use the power, but set a goal after which I relinquish it.

title: The unfinished answer
text: A teacher says every life must serve one purpose. You have found several that conflict.

choices.text: Choose one for now, without calling the others mistakes.
Build a life in which several purposes can take turns.
Ask why a life must justify itself through purpose.
Choose the purpose that helps the people relying on me.

title: The blank page
text: The Atlas offers to write the ending you deserve. It asks you to define deserve.

choices.text: An ending I chose while allowing others their choices.
An ending where fewer people must suffer for our safety.
An ending that tells the truth, even about my failures.
No ending yet. Leave something unwritten.

reflection.text: You have already considered what returning home might cost. What should an ending offer instead?
